blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: A neutron is stable only inside a nucleus. Free neutrons decay with a half-life of 900 s.

blocks.alt: A green sphere n on the left and a thick red arrow pointing right. Beyond the arrow: an orange sphere p at the top with a small arrow pointing up and to the left; a small grey sphere at the right labelled ν̄ (antineutrino) with an arrow pointing right; and a small grey sphere at the bottom labelled e⁻ with an arrow pointing down and to the left.
blocks.caption: Decay of a free neutron into a proton, an electron and an antineutrino (original drawing after the textbook's uncaptioned picture in the Do you know? box).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: A free neutron's half-life is about 610 s (about 10 minutes). About 880 s (nearly 15 minutes) is its mean lifetime, not its half-life.
